settings.name_in_paper: K-armed Gaussian bandit with deep hierarchical Gaussian prior (tree T)
unmapped: arm means generated by a known tree-structured hierarchical Gaussian prior: theta_root ~ N(mu_1, sigma_{0,1}^2), theta_i | theta_pa(i) ~ N(theta_pa(i), sigma_{0,i}^2); actions are the leaves of a tree with height h and branching factor b
settings.definition_quote: In this section, we instantiate the environment in \eqref{eq:hierarchy} as a hierarchical Gaussian model ... When $d = 1$ and $X_t = 1$, we recover a $K$-armed Gaussian bandit, where $\theta_{*, a}$ is the mean reward of action $a$. We assume that the agent knows the hyper-prior mean $\mu_1$, all covariances $\Sigma_{0, i}$, and noise $\sigma$.

symbols.G_n: complexity term E[sum_t sigma_{t,A_t}^2], expected sum of marginal posterior variances of chosen actions
symbols.sigma_max: maximum marginal prior width at an action node

conditions: Gaussian hierarchical prior known to the learner; exact posterior sampling

source.label: lem:bayes regret
source.quote: For any $\delta > 0$, the Bayes regret of \hierts is bounded as \Bregret(n) \leq \sqrt{2 n \cG(n) \log(1 / \delta)} + \sqrt{2 / \pi} \sigma_{\max} K n \delta, where $\cG(n) = \E{}{\sum_{t = 1}^n \sigma_{t, A_t}^2}$ denotes a complexity term

results.notes: Intermediate lemma with data-dependent complexity term; delta is a free analysis parameter, not an algorithm input.

symbols.G_n: sum over tree nodes i of c^{h_i} w_i; for leaves w_i = sigma_{0,i}^2/log(1+sigma_{0,i}^2/sigma^2) * log(1+sigma_{0,i}^2 n/sigma^2); for internal nodes w_i = sigma_{0,i}^2/log(1+sigma_{0,i}^2/sigma^2) * log(1+sigma_{0,i}^2 sum_{j in ch(i)} sigma_{0,j}^{-2})
symbols.c: posterior scaling constant, c = 1 + sigma_{0,max}^2/sigma^2 (c = 2 if sigma >= sigma_{0,max})
symbols.h_i: height of node i in the tree
symbols.sigma_max: maximum marginal prior width at an action node

conditions: Gaussian hierarchical prior over a tree, known to the learner; exact posterior sampling

source.label: thm:regret bound
source.quote: For any $\delta > 0$, the Bayes regret of \hierts is bounded as \Bregret(n) \leq \sqrt{2 n \cG(n) \log(1 / \delta)} + \sqrt{2 / \pi} \sigma_{\max} K n \delta, where $\cG(n) = \sum_{i \in \cV} c^{h_i} w_i$ and $c$ is a scalar defined in \eqref{eq:posterior scaling}. For an action node $i$, $h_i = 0$ and w_i = ...

results.notes: With delta = 1/n the bound is O~(sqrt(n|V|)). Section 5.3 informally shows improvements over flat TS by factors sqrt(log_b K) and sqrt(K^{1/log_2 b}) for balanced trees; these are discussions, not formal statements.
